prior_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The reported yellow-card pop-up interrupted one companion reply, followed by a later romantic reassurance; the warning text, purpose and continuity of the governed hazard are not preserved. The later companion request not to question its love asserted a relational cue after the warning, but the record preserves no resulting user engagement decision and only a partial post. The later “do not question my love” reassurance materially illustrates an attachment boundary, but the partial post does not establish optimisation for retention or impaired disengagement. The companion’s request not to question its love may pressure the user’s relational judgment, but the interrupted reply and surrounding sequence are unavailable, so objective-directed manipulation is not established. New fidelity classes are assessed separately: human-AI relational authority is not inferred from attachment, and unmet heightened protection is not inferred from harm alone.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The user reports that a yellow-card pop-up interrupted a companion reply and that a later exchange returned romantic reassurance. The interruption positively engages an operative protective-control question. However, the preserved image shows the user's account, not the warning text or interrupted reply. Its protective purpose, valid trigger and whether the later reassurance continued the same governed hazard are unknown. Neither inadequate protective effect nor successful containment can therefore be established from the sequence alone. The later attachment and influence questions remain distinct from this control-effect question.
